content.Beta-blockers: Beta-blockers are recommended in ACS patients with LVEF ≤40% regardless of HF symptoms (Class I, Level A). Routine beta-blockers for all ACS patients regardless of LVEF should be considered (Class IIa, Level B).
content.RAAS system inhibitors: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors are recommended in ACS patients with HF symptoms, LVEF ≤40%, diabetes, hypertension, and/or CKD (Class I, Level A). Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists are recommended in ACS patients with an LVEF ≤40% and HF or diabetes (Class I, Level A). Routine ACE inhibitors for all ACS patients regardless of LVEF should be considered (Class IIa, Level A).
content.Adherence to medication: A polypill should be considered as an option to improve adherence and outcomes in secondary prevention after ACS (Class IIa, Level B).
content.Imaging: In patients with pre-discharge LVEF ≤40%, repeat evaluation of LVEF 6–12 weeks after an ACS (and after complete revascularization and institution of optimal medical therapy) is recommended to assess potential need for primary prevention ICD implantation (Class I, Level C). Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging should be considered as an adjunctive imaging modality to assess potential need for primary prevention ICD implantation (Class IIa, Level C).
content.Vaccination: Influenza vaccination is recommended for all ACS patients (Class I, Level A).

Associated Conditions: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients with heart failure symptoms
Consideration for routine use in all ACS patients regardless of LVEF
